subject: HelixCare showcase synthesis & next tests
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@helixcare.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@helixcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: HelixCare showcase + proposed validation matrix

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk us through HelixCare's operational constraints and the areas you want to validate in the vendor showcase. Quick recap from our side so the team is aligned and so we can lock the POC entry criteria: 

Pain points (as described):
- Model inference latency spikes during peak API traffic (affects live triage UX)
- High per-token cost for longer context windows (long patient notes)
- Need for stronger data isolation and audit trails for PHI-sensitive traces

Goals for the next 6–8 weeks:
- Latency under 100ms p95 for the patient-triage endpoint at 5k concurrent users
- Cost target: <0.6 USD per 1k tokens after batching/quantization gains
- Full request/audit logging with KMS integration for stored artifacts

Decision criteria you called out:
1) Performance: p95 latency & throughput resiliency
2) Security/compliance: KMS + audit log fidelity
3) Operational simplicity: rollout controls and canary fallback
4) Unit economics at projected volume

Competitive context: you mentioned CloudBox and NimbusAI as other vendors in the run. We'll focus our POC on the three axes above so you can run apples-to-apples tests. Attached is a suggested validation matrix (helixcare-poc-matrix.xlsx) and a short recording of today's demo (redwood-demo-recording-20250709.mp4).

Proposed next steps & owners (suggested):
- Redwood provides POC scripts and test harness by Friday (owner: me)
- HelixCare to provision test dataset and KMS staging credentials (owner: Tom)
- Run baseline performance tests (no batching) followed by optimized runs (Redwood will run both)
- Procurement to share our template SOW/term sheet and any redlines (owner: procurement@helixcare.com)

Timing: We propose kicking the test window 2025-07-15 to 2025-07-21. If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and a Doc with concrete test commands.

Open questions we flagged:
- Do you require an on-prem agent vs VPC-hosted traffic for the POC?
- Any regulatory/regimen required for data de-identification prior to handing us sample traces?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the test harness and the Drive folder link by end of day.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment(s): helixcare-poc-matrix.xlsx; redwood-demo-recording-20250709.mp4
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@helixcare.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: HelixCare showcase + proposed validation matrix

Thanks, Jasmine — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) POC data: we'll provide a de-identified dump of the last 30 days of triage traffic. Tom will share the staging KMS creds by Friday.
2) On-prem vs VPC: For the initial performance runs we want VPC-hosted (no on-prem agent). If Redwood needs network peering instructions we'll provide them.
3) Compliance ask: SOC 2 Type II report and logging examples — can you confirm you'll attach those to the SOW?
4) Decision weighting: Performance 40%, Security/Compliance 30%, Cost 20%, Integration effort 10%.

Procurement is CC'd — they will review the term sheet and get back with any redlines. We also expect CloudBox to provide a proposal — would appreciate a short note on where Redwood expects to be weaker/stronger vs CloudBox so we can slot test cases.

Quick answer on timeline: 2025-07-15 test start is fine. We'll lock schedule once we have the test harness and the KMS staging creds.

Sarah Lee
Head of Clinical Ops | HelixCare
sarah.lee@helixcare.com

Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: HelixCare showcase + proposed validation matrix

Looping internal folks in with a focused plan for the comparative runs. Jasmine pointed out the right decision axes. From a competitive standpoint (vs CloudBox/NimbusAI) the initial hypotheses are: 

- Runtime performance: Redwood should have an edge in p95 tail latency with KV/prefix caching and continuous batching; we need to show headroom at 5k concurrent users. Test: scripted ramp to 5k with patient-like payloads. Owner: Karthik.
- Cost: CloudBox advertises cheaper list pricing for long contexts; our leverage will be quantized model profiles + batching. Test: identical corpus, measure tokens consumed and average cost per 1k tokens. Owner: Marissa.
- Security/compliance: Redwood supports KMS integration and auditing out of the box. Provide a sample audit log with a mapped event taxonomy. Owner: Jasmine (we'll attach SOC2 Type II and sample logs to the SOW).

I've attached a trimmed comparison matrix to the Drive (not attached here) and our draft term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-v1.pdf). Action items (short):
- Jasmine: finalize test harness + push to Drive by EOD Thu (owner: Jasmine)
- Karthik: build the load scripts (ramp + steady-state) and smoke runs by Mon 7/14 (owner: Karthik)
- Marissa: compile cost projection templates vs CloudBox using HelixCare traffic profile (owner: Marissa)

One practical ask: Sarah/Tom — can you confirm whether the test VPC allows outbound telemetry to our observability endpoint (we can also run telemetry via an observable endpoint in your VPC if required). That affects how we capture p95 tails.

I'll be conservative on the messaging to procurement — give them the term sheet and SOC2, ask for their window for redlines.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
